keyA.notes: Page 049 opens with a new # heading, so no '+' marker; p048 has no footnotes, so no (تابع). None of pp.050-052 continues the previous page (each previous page ends a sentence/paragraph). Allah: where a case vowel is printed after the font's automatic shadda+small-alif ligature (اللهَ on pp.049, 052) I wrote only the printed vowel: اللهَ; the bare ligature is الله / بِالله. p049 heading written 'الورد اليومي (الأساس)' (the gap after د is narrow in the bold title font; STRUCTURE gives two words). p049 bullets '*' kept as the printed asterisk glyph. p050: 'وتقسم على جميع الحاضرين.' is a bold standalone sentence ending in '.', so I wrote a bold paragraph, not a heading. p050 'في الملمات ... بالتلقي:' and the following Tazi salawat are one paragraph (the line before is full width, the next has no indent and no extra leading). Likewise p051 'أربع مرات.' closes the preceding paragraph. p051 heading: shadda above and kasra below the ص of الصِّديقي (bold title font). The intro line يُقْرَأُ … under the p051 title is a plain paragraph per STRUCTURE §2, even though it is set bold. The Quran ref '[الأعراف:٨٩].' is printed without spaces and is kept so. Other unusual vowelling kept as printed: اللَّهُمّ (shadda only, p051), كلُّه (bare kaf, p051), وَحْدَك / سَيِّدنَا / إِني (p051), الغَيبِ, وَالأرْضِ, إِلَه, دَعْوةِ, الأَرْض (p052), الخَوَاتِيْم (p050). quran.py raised no flags.

keyB.notes: p049 opens with the # heading after p048's complete list, so there is no '+'. p048 has no footnotes, so there is no (تابع). The pages 050, 051 and 052 each start a new indented paragraph after a complete sentence, so none has a '+'. Bullets are printed as a flower asterisk and written '* ' (CONVENTIONS §7, STRUCTURE). The word الله: wherever the plain font ligature is used, it is written الله, and only a separately printed case fatha is added (اللهَ on p049 and p052), as in earlier keyB batches (b12 اللهِ). Final ى carrying the font's automatic small alif is written as plain ى (عَلَى، إلى، ترضى، مَضَى، تُقْضَى، أَقْصَى، إِلَى). p050: the Tazi salat line «اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ صَلاةً…» starts flush right with no indent, and the line before it («…وصيغتها بالتلقي:») is full width. Per §6 it is joined to the «في الملمات…» paragraph. In the same way, on p051 «أربع مرات.» is joined to the preceding dua, and the reference «[الأعراف:٨٩].», which wraps onto its own line, stays with the Quran quotation. p050 «وتقسم على جميع الحاضرين.» is a bold standalone instruction, written as a **bold** paragraph. p051: the paragraph «يُقْرَأُ مرة في الصباح…» under the title is set in bold, but per STRUCTURE §2 a «تقرأ…» line under a title is a plain paragraph, so no ** was used. The calligraphic basmala is written in the standard form outside the brackets. The Quran text (الأعراف ٨٩) matches Tanzil with no tatweel before the dagger alif. In the lam-alif ligature the hamza of لأ sits on the left slanted stroke, which identifies that stroke as the alif. The fathatan above that stroke in «أَعْمَالاً» (p051) is therefore encoded on the alif. «لَمْ يَشَأ لَمْ يَكُنْ» (p052) is set tight, but each word is written separately with a space. All lines were checked against 650 dpi half-line renders and 1300 dpi third-line renders, plus 1500–3600 dpi zooms of every questionable mark (scratch\b13_*.png).
